Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ yo female with a history of multiple 
sclerosis, ulcerative colitis, and asthma who presented with a 
rapid decline in strength and level of consciousness and found 
to have Primary CNS B cell lymphoma after stereotactic brain 
biopsy. Her course was complicated by DVT, probable PE, and 
pneumonia.

Active Diagnoses:
# Primary CNS B cell lymphoma: Ms. ___ was transfered from 
___ to the ___. Her MRI was entered into our 
system. She was on Decadron for cerebral edema. Her speech 
became more slurred during the night and Decadron was increased 
to 10mg Q6 hours. Mannitol was started. CT head was done to rule 
out hemorrhage as her exam was dramatically worse then what was 
portrayed in the transfer notes. It was negative for hemorrhage 
but showed a frontotemporal mass.  She was started on Dilantin 
on the neurology service given seizure at OSH. With medical 
management her exam improved with less weakness on her left. 
Neuromedicine requested a biopsy due to the fact that review of 
OSH records revealed an LP that did not suggest MS. ___ were 
concerned for tumor. On the night of ___, she was taken to the 
OR on ___ for a stereotactic brain biopsy.  Preliminary 
pathology was reviewed with Heme-Path and thought to be primary 
CNS B-cell lymphoma. Postoperative CT head demonstrated mild 
pneumocephalus and small amount of acute blood products in the 
area of the biopsy. Patient was transferred to the Neuro-SDU.  
Her exam remained stable. On ___, patient was transferred to 
the floor.  She continued on high dose steroids.  Over the next 
several days her exam improved with improvement of her left 
facial droop and left-sided weakness. She was transitioned from 
Dilantin to Keppra for seizure prophylaxis. Her dexamethasone 
was tapered to dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily without further 
taper for the next week. She will be readmitted to the service 
next week on ___ for chemotherapy and second dose of 
methotrexate.

# DVT/PE: Patient developed pleuritic right sided 
chest/abdominal pain and tachycardia. It was suspected that she 
had a PE, so lower extremity ultrasound was obtained which 
confirmed left lower extremity DVTs. Unable to perform CTA chest 
 given concern for contrast affecting renal function while 
dosing MTX. Patient was treated with heparin drip then 
transitioned to Lovenox for discharge. She was given dilaudid as 
needed for pain control. 

# Health care associated pneumonia: Patient developed fever and 
hypoxia during her hospital course and was found to have right 
pleural effusion and bilateral opacities worrisome for 
pneumonia. Patient was treated for HCAP with cefepime and 
vancomycin. She is discharged with a PICC line and will continue 
cefepime and vancomycin for 4 more days with last dose to be 
completed on ___ to complete an eight day course. She 
remained afebrile for >48 hours prior to discharge. 

# Constipation: Most likely secondary narcotics and inactivity. 
Pt was given senna, colace, miralax, in addition to prn 
lactulose.  

# Abdominal pain: Likely referred from right-sided pleuritic 
pain as discussed above. CT abdomen showed no acute process. 
Pt's pain improved when treated for thrombosis and pneumonia. 

# Anemia: No active s/s of bleeding. Most likely related to 
phlebotomy, acute illness and MTX treatment. 

Inactive Diagnoses:
# Ulcerative colitis: Held Mesalamine and discharged with plan 
to continue to hold for now given as it can interfere with 
methotrexate.

# Asthma: No signs of exacerbation. Continue singulair, advair, 
albuterol prn.

radiology_notes.text:
STUDY:  MRI of the head with contrast, WAND protocol.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ woman with newly diagnosed right
ring-enhancing lesion, presurgical evaluation.

TECHNIQUE:  Post-gadolinium contrast axial images were obtained through the
brain in axial T1, sagittal MP-RAGE and multiplanar reconstructions were
provided and reviewed.

FINDINGS:  Unchanged large heterogeneously enhancing lesion is redemonstrated
in the right frontal subcortical region, with significant associated vasogenic
edema and mass effect, measuring approximately 49 x 53 mm in transverse
dimension, and causing approximately 11 mm of midline shifting towards the
left.  There is no evidence of significant change since the most recent study.
Fiducial markers are in place.  The possibility of a tumefactive demyelinating
lesion, primary brain tumor or metastases are considerations. There is a 8 mm
by 11 mm area of enhancement in the right cerebellum with an associated  thin
vessel (images #7, #8, series #3), possibly related with a developmental
venous anomaly, previously demonstrated on ___. No other lesions are
demonstrated since the most recent study.

IMPRESSION: 1. Unchanged heterogeneously enhancing lesion in the right frontal
region with significant edema in the basal ganglia and mass effect as
described above.  Fiducial markers are in place.

2. Unchanged right cerebellar enhancing lesion with mild vascular enhancement,
adjacent to the cerebellar nodule on the right, possibly consistent with a
developmental venous anomaly, a second lesion in this region cannot be
completely ruled out.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with a new left-sided weakness, confusion and
speech difficulties.

COMPARISON:  Reference MRI from an outside hospital ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT imaging of the head was obtained without an
intravenous contrast.  Sagittal and coronal reformations were performed and
reviewed.

FINDINGS:  There is a large hypodense lesion measuring approximately 4 cm
centered within the right frontotemporal lobes, with extensive surrounding
vasogenic edema.  This mass is better assessed in the earlier MRI study. 
There is significant mass effect on the right lateral ventricle, with leftward
shift of approximately 8 mm.  There is mild dilation of the left lateral
ventricle and left temporal horn suggesting a trapped ventricle.  There is
subfalcine and uncal herniation, and mild crowding at the foramen magnum.
There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage.

There is moderate opacification of bilateral ethmoid air cells.  Moderate
mucosal thickening is seen in the right maxillary sinus.  The patient is
status post right mastoid surgery.  The left mastoid air cells are clear.

IMPRESSION:  A large right frontotemporal mass with extensive surrounding
vasogenic edema and mass effect and leftward shift of midline structures to
approximately 8 mm.  Subfalcine and uncal herniation.  The above findings in
conjunction with the prior MRI are concerning for a tumefactive multiple
sclerosis or a primary malignant tumor (including primary versus secondary). 
The above findings were discussed with ___, at approximately
1:30 a.m. and immediately after the CT study.

CHEST ON ___

HISTORY:  Asthma, brain lesion, pre-op.

FINDINGS:  There are no old films available for comparison.  There is a
scoliosis involving the upper thoracic spine concaved left.  The lungs are
clear without infiltrate or effusion.  Cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are
normal.

CHEST ON ___

HISTORY:  Dobbhoff placement.

FINDINGS:  There is a new feeding tube with the tip just below the
gastroesophageal junction.  This should be advanced prior to being used for
feeding.  Again, seen is the scoliosis involving the upper thoracic spine. 
The lungs are clear.

CHEST ON ___

HISTORY:  Dobbhoff repositioned.

FINDINGS:  The Dobbhoff tube has been advanced slightly but is still in the
mid stomach, not far enough to be used for feeding.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with right frontal mass for stereotactic
biopsy.

COMPARISON:  Serial prior exams, dating to ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Incomplete study, with only "pre-contrast" axial FLAIR and T1
images obtained.

FINDINGS:  Re-demonstrated is the large right frontal mass with extensive
perilesional vasogenic edema.  Mass effect with distortion of the right
lateral ventricle and midline shift is somewhat reduced when compared to the
prior.  Rim-like T1-hyperintensity conforms to the region of previous
peripheral contrast enhancement, and most likely represents pooling of
residual contrast from previous exams, in region of blood-brain barrier
breakdown.  

On FLAIR images, additional changes in the posterior fossa with bilateral
signal abnormality involving the middle cerebellar peduncles as well as
adjacent to the cerebellar nodulus are more conspicuous, possibly also related
to pooling phenomena from previous contrast administration.

There are no new FLAIR-hyperintense foci identified.

Again seen is fluid retention in the right frontal sinus and ethmoid air
cells.

IMPRESSION:  Incomplete scan, re-demonstrating the complex right frontal mass
and posterior FLAIR signal abnormalities.  While the degree of mass effect
with distortion of the right lateral ventricle and midline shift appears
improved, peripheral ring-like T1-hyperintensity at the margin of the lesion
may be explained on the basis of residual contrast-pooling phenomenon.

INDICATION:  Planning for stereotactic brain biopsy of right frontal mass.

COMPARISON:  Serial prior exams, the most remote dated ___, obtained at
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MP-RAGE as well as axial T1 spin echo were obtained on a
stereotactic frame with contrast.

FINDINGS:

When compared to the study obtained in early ___, there is interval reduction
in size of the right frontal ring-enhancing mass lesion, decreased from
previous 4.5 x 5.9 cm, to current 3.6 x 4.7 mm in the axial imaging plane. 
Thickness of ring-like enhancing tissue is likewise decreased and degree of
mass effect on the right lateral ventricle, moderately improved. Associated
vasogenic edema involving the right frontal and parts of the temporal lobe is
grossly unchanged.

Redemonstrated is another enhancing lesion in the right cerebellar hemisphere,
adjacent to the cerebellar nodule, which most likely represents a second
manifestation of the same disease.

No additional or new focus of enhancement are identified.

There is no new hydrocephalus and no evidence of interval hemorrhage.

Again seen is fluid retention in the right frontal sinus and ethmoid air
cells.

IMPRESSION:
1. Limited study for surgigal planning showing mild interval improvement in
the ring-enhancing mass in the left frontal lobe with reduction in degree of
mass effect.

2. Relatively stable appearance of right cerebellar enhancing focus,
suggesting multifocal disease.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman status post right brain biopsy.

COMPARISON:  CT ___ and multiple MRIs from ___ through ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast MDCT axial images were acquired through the head.

FINDINGS:  The patient is status post right frontal burr hole for biopsy. 
There is a small amount of right frontal pneumocephalus.  Hyperdense material
adjacent to a focus of pneumocephalus (3:18) likely represents a small amount
of acute blood after biopsy.  Edema in the right frontotemporal lobe is
similar to the recent CT, corresponding to the region of known mass lesion
better delineated on MRI ___. There is 8 mm leftward shift of normally
midline structures, previously 14 mm on CT ___ and unchanged from MRI
earlier today.  The suprasellar cistern and quadrigeminal plate cisterns are
patent.  The perimesencephalic cisterns are mildly effaced, improved from
___. The right cerebellar lesion is not well visualized on this study.  


A small mucus retention cyst is seen in the left maxillary sinus.  Ethmoid air
cell opacification is improved although aerosolized secretions in the right
sphenoid sinus are worse than on ___.  The patient is status post right
mastoid surgery.  The left mastoid air cells are clear.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Pneumocephalus and small amount of acute blood products in the right
frontal region after biopsy.
2.  Right frontotemporal edema due to large mass with subfalcine herniation,
better-delineated on MRI of earlier today. Mild effacement of the right
perimesencephalic cisterns is improved from ___.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST ___

INDICATIONS:  Rule out pneumonia.  Patient with history of CNS lymphoma and
pleuritic chest pain.

Exam compared to the chest ___.

FINDINGS:  New airspace opacities that are bilateral and bibasal, but more
prominent in the right lower lobe.  Mild pleural effusion on the right side. 
The mediastinal and cardiac contour are otherwise normal.  No edema, no
pneumothorax.  Mild scoliosis of the thoracic spine.

CONCLUSION:  New airspace consolidation at the base of both lungs, but more
prominent in the right lower lobe, suggestive of multifocal pneumonia or
aspiration.

HISTORY:  ___ female with B-cell lymphoma with new onset pleuritic
chest pain.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:  

There is normal respirophasic waveform in the bilateral common femoral veins,
with normal response to Valsalva.  Within the bilateral common femoral,
superficial femoral, and popliteal veins, there is normal compressibility,
color flow, and response to augmentation.  There is normal color flow and
compressibility within the posterior tibial and peroneal veins of the calf.  

Within the left gastrocnemius vein and soleus vein, there is echogenic
thrombus which is incompressible, without color flow.  This does not clearly
propagate to the posterior tibial or peroneal veins.

IMPRESSION:  

Deep venous thrombosis within the left gastrocnemius and soleus veins.

These findings were discussed with Dr. ___ at 5:10 p.m. by phone.

SINGLE FRONTAL VIEW OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Fever.  The patient with primary CNS lymphoma.

Comparison is made with prior study, ___.

There has been interval increase in small-to-moderate right pleural effusion. 
Bibasilar opacities have increased on the right, likely atelectasis; on the
left, they are worrisome for pneumonia.  There is no pneumothorax. 
Cardiomediastinal contours are unchanged.  There are low lung volumes.  There
is dilatation of bowel loops in the upper abdomen and dilatation of the
stomach.

HISTORY:  Primary CNS lymphoma, now bowel dilatation on chest x-ray.
Radiology resident, Dr. ___ further history that the patient
is asymptomatic and passing gas.

ABDOMEN, SINGLE SUPINE PORTABLE VIEW.

Gas and stool are seen throughout much of the colon, extending down to the
sigmoid and rectum.  In the region of the splenic flexure, the distal
transverse colon is  prominent, but not dilated (measuring 5.2 cm).  The
air-filled viscus in the left upper quadrant appears to represent a mildly
distended, but not frankly dilated stomach, displaced inferiorly by the liver.
Assessment for free air is limited on this supine film that excludes the
diaphragms and obturator foramina.  No obvious free air is identified.  Left
convex l-spine scoliosis noted.

IMPRESSION:  

Gas and stool throughout the colon, without frank dilatation to suggest
obstruction or ileus.

INDICATION:  History of CNS lymphoma and pulmonary embolism, now complaining
of increasing right-sided abdominal pain.  Please evaluate for
microperforation.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
following the administration of water-soluble oral contrast material.  No IV
contrast was administered.  Multiplanar reformats were performed.

COMPARISON:  None.

ABDOMEN CT:  There is a moderate right pleural effusion as well as a small
left pleural effusion.  Consolidative right lower lobe opacities may reflect
compressive atelectasis, although superimposed aspiration/infection is
certainly possible.  Similar, although less severe, left lower lobe
consolidative opacites are noted.  There is a trace pericardial fluid.

Lack of intravenous contrast material limits assessment of the abdominal
organs.  The liver is grossly unremarkable.  The gallbladder contains minimal
layering material, likely sludge. There is no gallbladder wall thickening. The
spleen is normal in size.  The pancreas is grossly normal.  The kidneys are
unremarkable.  The adrenal glands are grossly normal.  

The stomach and small bowel are unremarkable.  A large quantity of stool is
seen throughout the colon.  The appendix is not definitely visualized.  There
is no free fluid or free air in the abdomen.  No pathologically enlarged
abdominal lymph nodes are seen.  The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber. 
Scattered aortic calcifications are seen.

PELVIS CT:  The bladder is moderately distended but otherwise grossly normal. 
The uterus is unremarkable.  Bilateral ovarian follicles are noted.  There is
trace physiologic free fluid in the cul-de-sac.  No pathologically enlarged
pelvic lymph nodes are seen.

BONE WINDOW:  No suspicious lytic or blastic lesions are identified.  S-shaped
scoliosis of the thoracolumbar spine is seen.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intra-abdominal or intra-pelvic process.
3.  Bilateral lower lobe consolidative opacities, right greater than left,
possibly secondary to compressive atelectasis given the adjacent pleural
effusions, although infection or aspiration could have a similar appearance.
3.  Small quantity of sludge within the gallbladder.  No associated
gallbladder wall thickening to suggest acute cholecystitis.

STUDY:  AP CHEST, ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman with PICC line placement.

FINDINGS:  Comparison is made to the prior study from ___.

There has been placement of a right-sided PICC line whose distal tip is poorly
seen, however, is likely at the cavoatrial junction.  There are no
pneumothoraces.  There are bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than
left.  There is some atelectasis at the both lung bases with potential
developing infiltrate at the right lung base.  Overall, these findings are
